title: le_disasm — DOS LE/LX reassembly-oriented disassembler
reason: C++ libopcodes-based executable disassembler derived from swdisasm. It parses DOS MZ/LE/LX linear executable structures and emits AT&T/GAS-style assembly intended to support analysis and reassembly.

title: WebXpressionPlus X68000 browser modernization
reason: Modernization of Mitsuky's WebXpression native Human68k browser, adding UTF-8 to Shift-JIS conversion and TLS support while retaining HTML parsing, images/cache/history and 68k display routines.

title: Evoland GB
reason: Fan-made native Game Boy demake of Evoland. Source implements tile-map movement, player sword animation, chest activation and progressive controls/game features. This is a work-in-progress original implementation rather than an original-binary interpreter.

title: Fractint legacy — DOS source release reconstruction
reason: Historical source-release reconstruction/archive of DOS Fractint versions up to 19.6, preserving the Stone Soup Group fractal generator, optimized assembly arithmetic, graphics drivers and help compiler. This is source restoration rather than binary decompilation.

title: Man Over Board
reason: Original Atari ST typing/rescue game whose model tracks swimmer movement, word rows, score and decorative state; includes native raster, PSG, interrupts and input code plus module tests.

title: Operation Jeff
reason: Mouse-aimed native Spectrum Next arcade defense game. Players eliminate approaching Jeffs using delayed explosions, charge management and numerous bonuses while advancing through areas.

title: worzxle
reason: Wordle-style five-letter word puzzle implemented for the ZX80, ZX81 and Spectrum/Timex family. Six guesses receive positional/letter feedback and feed a running score.

title: ZX Log Chopper
reason: Original compact Spectrum timing game: activate a moving chopper at log markers, earn round scores and progress through logs while maintaining a high score.

title: Castle Dungeon — Locomotive BASIC engine
reason: Native CPC didactic RPG/platform engine demonstration with tile map, limited camera window, collision, coins, doors/keys, enemies and combat scenes. Complete text BASIC listing is the substantive implementation.

title: Final Fantasy — ColecoVision C reimplementation
reason: Explicit native C/Z80 rewrite of NES Final Fantasy rules using Disch’s disassembly as specification and user-ROM extracted assets, not 6502 translation/emulation. Battle overlays, fixed-bank services, maps and quest state run through 512KB MegaCart banking with SGM RAM.

title: Fractal Explorer Falcon source
reason: Kochise’s archived native Atari Falcon030 Mandelbrot/Julia explorer. Full 68030/FPU assembler implementation controls the Falcon video mode, screen memory and blitter before computing fractal iterations.

title: NGPC Sound Creator
reason: C++/Qt tracker, piano-roll, instrument/SFX and project tool for native NGPC sound export. polling_driver.cpp supplies real Z80 polling-driver bytes and command host logic; project includes clean-room Z80/T6W28 preview cores and C/ASM output.

title: SITBOL — recovered PDP-10 SNOBOL4 implementation
reason: Recovered Stevens Institute SITBOL compiler/runtime modules, extracted from historical University of Arizona archive material, covering lexer, syntax, interpreter, strings, arrays, I/O and garbage collection.

title: TYMCOM-X — Tymshare PDP-10 operating-system source
reason: Substantial Tymshare PDP-10 monitor archives with scheduler, swapping/memory, filesystem, devices and many machine/site configuration variants, plus build control files and operational documentation.

title: VecNIST — native Vectrex digit recognizer
reason: Interactive Vectrex handwriting recognizer: joystick or experimental light-pen stroke input, 12×12 integer rasterization and a 144–64–10 neural network running on the console CPU. vecnist.asm implements drawing, scaling, first-layer accumulation, second-layer multiplication and score displays; weights and training/test twins are supplied.

title: Bob’s Fury
reason: Ongoing Pascal version of Andrew Danson’s DOS platform game, started around 1999 and retaining levels from his earlier QBasic version. Includes engine, XT and standard builds, level editor, graphics modes and sound drivers.

title: PointDBF 96 Delphi password-dialog component
reason: Author-published source accompanying Patrick Prémartin’s January 1999 PointDBF article: a Delphi VCL login/password-change component and demonstration applications, with event hooks for application-defined password handling.

title: Smalltalk-80 by the Book — Pharo-hosted VM
reason: Independent implementation of the complete Bluebook Smalltalk-80 VM and environment in Smalltalk itself, with Tonel-format interpreter, object memory, BitBlt, display and filesystem adapters for Pharo.

title: Airaki
reason: Full native tile-matching RPG/puzzle game released in 2014. Assembly contains horizontal/vertical matching, board solvability checks, combat, animation, sound and link multiplayer, with art and auxiliary checksum tool.

title: Checkers — OS/2 Presentation Manager source continuation
reason: Charles Petzold’s September 1990 Microsoft Systems Journal checkers game, preserved with its original sources and a 2026 Open Watcom 32-bit PM continuation. The implementation includes board/judge windows, legal-move generation, recursive jump enumeration and a threaded computer strategy.

title: LGP-ASM — Go symbolic LGP-30 assembler
reason: Compact independent Go assembler for LGP-30 source with labels, opcode/order table, literal packing, multiple number notations, two-pass symbol replacement and native-word emission. Unit tests exercise literals and parsing; implemented tool distinct from the author’s browser-emulator code.

title: LISP 1.5 — IBM 7090 card-deck reconstruction
reason: Pascal Bourguignon reconstructs the 1961 IBM 7090 LISP 1.5 punched-card source from Bonnie’s Birthday Assembly listing, preserving card layout and known typographical quirks while generating some tables and inferring five obscured cards. Includes original listing PDF, reconstructed assembly, generator Lisp, assembler patches and run recipe.

title: m100LE — Wordle for Model 100 family
reason: Commented native BASIC Wordle-like game for Tandy Model 100 and related Kyocera/NEC/Olivetti machines, with compressed yearly dictionaries and platform-specific terminal/date handling.

title: MSXgl — native MSX game library and build tools
reason: Configurable C/Z80 game-development runtime covering MSX graphics, input, audio, storage and memory banking, plus build and asset tools. Many sample games/demos are examples within one reusable library project.

title: Princess and Frog — Ed Fries Atari source release
reason: Preservation release of Ed Fries’ Romox Atari 8-bit game, with original source disk and Kay Savetz’s exported text files. Kept as one source-release family.

title: Zoo Clean / Zoo Care
reason: Native Amstrad CPC zoo-themed action/collection game in C. The source menu calls it Zoo Clean (and retains Scape text), while repository is zoo-care. Gameplay includes directional movement, bait/attack controls, guard/enemy state behavior, collectibles, cage-opening objectives, lives and level changes.

title: Cornwell Smalltalk-80 — custom-bytecode clone
reason: Richard Cornwell's Smalltalk-80 clone based on the Blue Book, with a simplified/custom VM, C bootstrap compiler, native Smalltalk compiler, object memory, image snapshots and a partly finished graphical interface.

title: inty-midi — MIDI to IntyBASIC music converter
reason: Haskell MIDI importer and converter that maps instruments, quantizes time and allocates available voices, producing IntyBASIC MUSIC statements or a standalone preview program for Intellivision/ECS.

title: PC98IMEBridge — Windows IME to PC-98 input bridge
reason: Windows .NET input window and native FreeDOS(98) resident program transmit committed Japanese input into PC-98 BIOS keyboard queues. Contains serial protocol, TSR hooks, IRQ buffering and a device-driver alternative.

title: Zombie Near — MSX and ColecoVision source release
reason: Oscar Toledo’s original Zombie Near action game source release, preserving dated development snapshots and native platform versions. The ColecoVision game contains its own Z80 game loop, enemy AI, maps and SN76489 music rather than emulating an existing game.

title: ADVGEN 1991 adventure compiler and interpreter
reason: Original 1991 QuickBASIC text-adventure compiler/interpreter re-released by its author, including a small HOUND demonstration and original source/project files. Distinct historical author network.

title: GPM/CLR — Gardens Point Modula-2 compiler for CLR
reason: Gardens Point Modula-2 compiler frontend with a CIL emitter, preserving the historical compiler lineage while enabling unmanaged Modula-2 applications on .NET. Source includes semantic traversal, parser, CIL writer and C# runtime modules.

title: JUDAS Apocalyptic Softwaremixing Soundsystem
reason: Preservation repository for the historical JUDAS 2.10d DOS sound library: module/sample playback, software mixers and direct Sound Blaster, GUS, AC97 and HDA hardware support.

title: Snake Megadrive — native SGDK game source
reason: Native Sega Mega Drive Snake implementation in C/SGDK. game.c implements directional steering, level speed, edge/wrap checks, food/bonus placement and self-collision; linked-list body, menu, game-over and win modules accompany graphics/audio resources.

title: Timebomb — VIC-20 BASIC-to-assembly remake
reason: Dave Curran’s 2026 6502 rewrite of Doug Smoak’s July 1983 Compute! BASIC type-in game. Original BASIC listing and magazine scans accompany the implementation.

title: Pokémon Trading Card Game
reason: RGBDS disassembly with documented US ROM and patch identities, assembly instructions and CI. Matching is author-documented, not independently verified here.

title: ShareFS compatible server
reason: Native ShareFS protocol implementation for modern hosts serving RISC OS clients. README documents x64/arm64 builds; GPL-3.0-only. Scoped Copilot instructions are present.

title: chaossource/menace-reverse-engineering
reason: Defer claimed complete Menace port: README and COMPLETED claims conflict with unfinished original logic; actual game.cpp uses generic timed random enemies and placeholder rendering, while disassembly helper slices guessed disk offsets. Concrete tools exist, but faithful reconstruction and reliable extraction claims are not established. Do not promote completion rhetoric as game restoration.

title: cycl0ne/DungeonMasterTools
reason: Defer canonical-host migration check: GitHub README explicitly says the project moved to Codeberg, where graphics.dat support was added. The GitHub Python dungeon parser and example are concrete, but the destination was inaccessible in this review; retain the canonical source lead rather than silently track an obsolete mirror as current.

title: sndhfix — SNDH music-file diagnostics
reason: Host-side SNDH diagnostics parses metadata and subtunes, checks termination/bounds and converts Atari text to Unicode; source includes ICE support. Current CLI reads and prints files, not an automatic music repair or playback claim.

title: Large CLI — early Amiga PAL window utility
reason: Historical utility enlarges the boot CLI by 56 vertical pixels using Intuition window sizing. Actual small assembly implementation inspected.

title: CAMD Tools — Amiga Doom MIDI integration
reason: Doom sound forwarding library and CAMD/MUS playback tools provide native MIDI integration. Reviewed library exports and build targets.

title: H-TRON — DOS graphics and GEM ports
reason: Extends RobertK’s Hercules Tron game to CGA/EGA/VGA and GEM, with Amstrad PC 1512/1640 joystick support.

title: GB2CPC — Game Boy source-port compatibility layer
reason: Early GBDK-style API and Mode-1 tile/palette conversion library, with virtual OAM and a small moving-sprite example.

title: fabbricius/olaftic
reason: Only a README announces an OLAF TIC-80 port; no implementation or original creator release is available here.

title: Breakout.ACC and Breakout+ — Atari ST reconstruction
reason: Disassembly-derived C accessory and patched assembly fix timing, window lifecycle and multitasking issues; Plus adds resizing and other extensions.

title: Block Breaker — MSX BASIC game
reason: Readable BASIC paddle/ball game with explicit collision, velocity, scoring and sound code, alongside disk distribution and design documents.

title: Apple II Forth Animation Demo — original Forth source
reason: Recovered circa1983/84 animation demonstration with readable Forth definitions and embedded 6502 assembler words.

title: Modern Biology: Respiration — original Forth source
reason: Original commercial Forth educational program; readable overlay code names glycolysis, Krebs cycle and electron-transport modules.

title: Drawing DataTypes — DR2D and SVG superclass
reason: Native drawing superclass and DR2D/SVG datatype implementations provide structured vector-art loading/rendering.

title: readhunk — minimal native-endian Hunk inspector
reason: Small exploratory reader walks header/code/RELOC32/end records and prints layout information.

title: C64 BASIC Tokenizer — Python conversion
reason: Script constructs token bytes, line numbers and little-endian next-line links from textual BASIC.

title: m68000 — Rust CPU interpreter and instruction tools
reason: Motorola 68000 interpreter, decoder and dynamic instruction emitter with MC68000/SCC68070 behavior profiles and C bindings.

title: ubox MSX — C game support libraries
reason: BIOS wrapper, sprite/pattern manager and Arkos AKM music/effect integration support Screen 2 game development.

title: Dunk Shot — MSX2 sprite-flicker patch
reason: Patch ports sprite presentation to SCREEN4/mode2 on MSX2, disables the old sprite-sharing scheme and preserves an MSX1 conditional path.

title: PIC2SPR — GIF to MSX2 mode2 sprite data
reason: Delphi utility converts a 256x16 sixteen-color GIF strip to sprite-mode2 pattern/color tables with BLOAD output.

title: Hippel Z80 — Atari music replay conversion
reason: Jochen Hippel/Mad Max sound driver converted from 68000 to Z80, retaining original sound data structures.

title: 1977 — retro text-mode art and Apple II export
reason: Native Mac art converter uses platform fonts/palettes and includes Apple II BASIC/ProDOS export; concrete block allocation and disk-writing implementation inspected.

title: Spectrumizer — MIDI and PT3 conversion
reason: Arranges MIDI into three-channel AY/PT3 data, recovers PT3 notes to MIDI, auditions and packages self-playing tape/snapshot outputs.

title: SimAnt DOS — partial historical matching reconstruction
reason: Recovered MSC6/RTLink-overlay game translation units with precise fixup/data ownership. Inspected an overlay source and generated progress report.

title: Blackthorne Reborn — engine and actor-script recovery
reason: Native C++ reconstructs original actor-bytecode interpreter and game flow using explicit data-segment layouts; Machine is a game-data model, not an x86 instruction interpreter.

title: Skepar/7-colors
reason: C game and AI implementations exist despite stale README TODO, but no inspected evidence ties algorithms to recovered original source or binary analysis. Not counted as restoration merely from reimplementation wording.

title: DuckTales: The Quest for Gold — Amiga source recovery
reason: Recovered Aztec C/assembly and typed-data accounting, with semantic map module and proof ledgers. Newer docs describe a 32-bit SDL3 compatibility port while the root README still says no independent build exists.

title: SkyNET and Future Shock — frozen Godot recovery
reason: Godot reimplements XnGine shooter rules and data decoding, including mission scripts, movers, destructibles, vehicles and game flow.

title: Inferno Engine — Java DOOM source port and format framework
reason: Java21/LWJGL/SDL3 framework includes substantive DOOM game-source port with original fixed-point simulation and named action dispatch. Inspected actor/weapon callback mapping.

title: anon569/AtariST-Little-Computer-People
reason: Verified GitHub fork of tracked sarnau/AtariST-Little-Computer-People. Same title and recovery identity; do not duplicate under fork owner.

title: dk8827/alleycat-remastered
reason: Browser remaster statically translates 8086 instructions into register/flag/segmented-memory execution with device modeling. Assembly recovery is present, but retain for explicit game-specific emulation audit rather than count as a native high-level rewrite.

title: SirL0LL0/amiga-m68k-decomp
reason: Reusable matching/decompilation pipeline, not an identified game/application restoration in inspected README. Retain for separate tooling pass instead of padding this focused batch.

title: Captain Comic II — annotated recovery and C++ reconstruction
reason: Annotated IDA disassembly and Ghidra cross-reference plus actual C++ player, entity, resource and renderer modules. Inspected player controller contains structured source, not just planned scaffolding.

title: GRimAce11/WaveformKit
reason: README and Swift AudioDecoder identify a modern general SwiftUI audio visualization package, not Spectrum tape recovery or retro development tooling. Search matched generic spectrum/tap/WAV terminology.

title: Nemesis / Gradius — bank-aware MSX reconstruction
reason: Sixteen-bank Konami4 disassembly uses whole-cartridge and per-bank control-flow tracing, anchored notes, graphics extraction and cross-checks for code/data conflicts.

title: bkbin2wav — Electronika BK tape-audio encoding
reason: Converts emulator BIN header/data into BK tape WAV with checksum, filename/address overrides and double-frequency turbo option.

title: seclorum/oscar64.oric
reason: GitHub metadata identifies fork of tracked drmortalwombat/oscar64. README retains upstream identity and reviewed tree/compiler source do not establish a distinct Oric implementation.

title: IMG2DISK — native Atari ST image restoration
reason: GFA BASIC program reads ST/MSA images, handles compressed tracks and writes/formats physical floppy tracks through Atari system calls.

title: Art1kDev/pole-chudes-mat
reason: Source header explicitly says code, tables and structure are identical to the base Pole Chudes recovery and only string constants differ. Record the historical text variant without adding another engine entry.

title: ZRDX — restored Zurenava DOS extender
reason: 1998-99 extender source modernized for NASM/Open Watcom/UPX with native LE/PE/RDOFF loaders and DPMI host; inspected original-attributed LE loader.

title: BOMBKI — Pascal matching recovery and native ports
reason: Recovered 1999 text RPG and units, with original-author-approved lineage from rzuf79/bombki. Inspected MONSTRA Pascal unit and TP7 conformance requirements.

title: ecomp — Amiga E compiler/interface reconstruction
reason: JavaScript compiler emits genuine 68k HUNK/ADF output; reverse-engineered EMOD/OOP ABI supports original binary modules. Inspected module reader and original-compiler comparison documentation.

title: Rayman DOS — matching C reconstruction
reason: GOG 1.21 reconstruction with 1.12/PS1/Rayverse semantic references; inspected Blacktoon logic and status separation.

title: Fallout 1 DOS Patcher — recovered engine patch system
reason: Implements DOS loader, relocatable patch payload and installer to bring selected Windows-era Fallout engine fixes to DOS executable.

title: Commander Keen 4 — reconstructed-source Tandy port
reason: Adapts reconstructed Keen 4 source for Tandy 16-color display/music, with MCGA/EGA/CGA variants and ZX0 compression to fit 720 KiB media.

title: Test Drive Enhanced — reconstructed driving core
reason: Extends faithful test-drive-sdl3 C core with high-resolution road rendering, longer draw distance and smooth presentation while retaining original simulation.

title: Amiga smbfs — upstream protocol reverse engineering
reason: Amiga SMBFS is a port of Sharity-Light SMB filesystem code. The cited reverse engineering concerns SMB network protocol behavior, while this repository does not analyze a retro Amiga disk, application, executable, or game format; an ordinary native filesystem port alone falls outside the catalogue’s archaeology/tooling scope.

title: Amiga Assembly Library — original source and C bindings
reason: Substantive original 1990s Amiga assembly.library code is present in public/download/asm, including the library resident/function table and implementations, plus C interfaces and examples. The enclosing modern documentation site and archive form one project.

title: coco-disasm
reason: Archived mirror points to GitLab; inspect the canonical history and current build state before promotion.

title: Hamazing / PLatOS canonical source scope
reason: Creator provenance and a substantive native demo/framework are established, but individual canonical build and implementation file retrieval failed. Inspect source/hamazing/build.bat and source/framework/framework_tasks.asm to verify exact target CPU, build output and framework capabilities before authoring the single root-scoped record. The retired GitHub README must not become the project destination.

title: blocklyvn8bit — non-promoted Amiga/C64 review
reason: README describes a work-in-progress mashup of BlocklyVN32X and 8Bit-Unity. Actual visual-novel runtime C source, project management and editor source exist. config.json names an external 8bit-Unity tree, but inspected vn32x.js still builds generated.32x via the older vn32x toolchain. C64-specific target integration has not been established strongly enough to accept this as a C64 project; require an explicit build target or primary support evidence. Apache-2.0 project metadata and inherited components; external 8Bit-Unity dependency. package.json has no real test script; no builds were run.

title: drhelius/Gearsystem
reason: Fresh SG-1000/SC-3000 code search resolved to the already indexed Gearsystem emulator/debugger record; it is not a new project.

title: fadden/6502bench
reason: Maintained interactive 6502-family disassembler/static-analysis workbench with assembler verification.

title: rep-stosw/tube64
reason: Distinct 64-bit successor implementation with source, build scripts and published binaries.

title: ucosty/blobbo
reason: Data-format reverse engineering and a level decoder/viewer only. The inspected BlobboGame class loads/decrypts levels; no playable game reconstruction or explicit 68k CPU proof was established. Keep as tooling context, not a game discovery.

title: FinalBurn-X
reason: Primary README presents a macOS frontend/port of FinalBurn Alpha; the reviewed repository does not establish a distinct retro-development or software-archaeology contribution.

title: Galaxian — Scott Tunstall arcade reverse engineering
reason: Primary repository documentation and implementation establish commented arcade-game reverse engineering listing within tracker scope.

title: yosshin4004/x68k_gcc_has_converter
reason: Primary README says this predecessor ended and its converter was integrated into xdev68k; preserve the lineage without creating a second active record.

title: pc88-disk-tools — NEC PC-8801 D88 disk-image utilities
reason: Primary README and implementation evidence establish the independently catalogued scope described by pc88-disk-tools — NEC PC-8801 D88 disk-image utilities.

title: txuswashere/Homebrew
reason: The repository describes a multi-system collection of homebrew ROMs but provides no source, author-level provenance or distinct development contribution in the inspected root documentation; a third-party binary collection is not promoted.

title: acornaeology/disassembly-skills
reason: Primary repository evidence establishes a distinct in-scope retro-development or software-archaeology project; the matching project audit records CPU, build, runtime and uncertainty boundaries explicitly.

title: Sargon II VIC-20 — annotated relocation and opening-book repair
reason: Annotated engine relocated to RAM, with optional Sargon 2.1 CP/M opening-book replacement. Source explains the original missing book-table byte and changed RESTORE behaviour; this is not an unchanged cartridge reconstruction.

title: Dec-ROM — scrambled EPROM bit-wiring recovery
reason: Manual address/data permutation and bounded heuristic Auto-Fix for scrambled EPROMs. Auto-Fix is explicitly Z80-only despite additional decoder modules; known wiring patterns are tried before general search. Confidence threshold is described as uncalibrated, not proof of universal recovery.

title: amiga-re-kit — measured Amiga reverse-engineering toolkit
reason: Game-agnostic extraction of instruments from SWIV, Turrican II and Superfrog projects. ADF/HUNK readers, checksum-aware unpackers, conservative 68000 walking, MCP and capture comparison are implemented. Recompiler is explicitly a prototype with a restricted blitter/custom-chip model; unmodelled accesses are logged, not proof of a complete native game port.

title: stjeanp/applesoft-basic-decompiler
reason: GitHub comparison with already tracked moralrecordings upstream is identical: zero ahead, zero behind. No distinct implementation to add.

title: Cyber Block Metal Orange — PC-98 English translation
reason: Two-disk translation rebuild handles PRECO on Disk A and FAT12 on Disk B, with input hash checks, script/image changes and IPS output. ERC VFD is a container, not an HDM rename; emulator in-memory saves require explicit flushing.

title: BBC Forth — Z80 second-processor port
reason: Port derived from Acornsoft Forth disassembly, retaining a 6502 host stub while running Forth on the Z80 second processor. Interactive but incomplete, with unit tests documented.

title: TapeRipper — native Oric tape-to-disk preservation
reason: Loads tape blocks on the original machine and writes numbered disk files; includes multipart and slow-tape modes. This is distinct from modern WAV decoding.

title: CPM-65 — 6502 operating system and utilities
reason: Author-maintained CP/M-like BIOS/BDOS/CCP and native utilities including assembler, BASIC and Forth. Nearly compatible disk directory is not 8080 binary compatibility; programs load at $0200.

title: Oric tools — preserved tape, disk and BASIC utilities
reason: Historical Euphoric-associated format tools include BASIC tokenization, assemblers, plotter rendering and disk conversion. This root adds smaller Sedoric-image configuration support. Empty primary README does not mean absent implementation.

title: Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days — DS matching-module reconstruction
reason: EU YKGP ARM9/overlay reconstruction reports all 306 modules matching, while distinguishing C, library assembly and two CLZ exceptions. Matching modules are not a playable rebuilt ROM; naming/structure consolidation remains ongoing and reported counters have different denominators.

title: GoldenEye tools — assets, maps, audio and debugging
reason: Coherent GoldenEye suite contains setup/stan conversion, Gebug64 tooling, C audio utilities and a browser map viewer. It is not a completed full game decompilation.

title: Street Fighter Alpha 2 — S-DD1-free reconstruction tools
reason: Pre-decompresses graphics and patches chip-arming sites to build 96 Mbit SFA2/Zero2 ROMs without S-DD1. Preserves side-effecting dummy stores and uses pinned hardware models; this is modified game output, not byte-identical retail ROM reconstruction.

title: Shin Taketori Monogatari — PC-88 BASIC protection tools
reason: Game-specific N88 BASIC decryption/encryption and extraction/insertion. Source annotates original Z80 operations; bank/address arguments and embedded keys are format-specific, not general cryptographic recovery.

title: SimsAdvanceRet/UrbzGBADecomp
reason: Inspected tree contains only a short README announcing a WIP. No recovered source, build or analysis artifact is present at this revision; retain as a lead rather than claim a source-bearing decompilation.

title: FPLAY — Compile PC-98 driver and sequence research
reason: Studies driver 2.11a and parses music banks into structured sequence listings, with FASM regeneration macros. Address-prefixed diagnostic listings explicitly cannot be recompiled.

title: dostoc — experimental DOS-to-C decompiler
reason: Source implements CFG/SSA/C-generation experiments with a udis86 wrapper. Author explicitly calls it broken/incomplete toy work, not a working arbitrary-DOS porting pipeline.

title: WinAPE load — CPCTelera Windows/WSL workflow
reason: Scripts bridge Linux/WSL builds to host Windows WinAPE, loading disk images and NOI symbols on changes. Not a new CPC emulator or game engine.

title: RetrolariumLab/solomon_no_kagi_src
reason: Already tracked as solomons-key-nes-reconstruction under oranguthang. Old API redirects to repository ID1352704779, identical to the selected root; preserve owner-rename lineage.

title: Mario Party 3 — N64 decompilation
reason: US ROM reconstruction; inspected entry C creates native libultra threads. Setup generates assembly for nonmatched functions, so buildability does not establish complete C recovery.

title: voodatari/Dogs-of-War-Atari-ST-Recomp-for-Windows
reason: BAKED EMULATION: generated C retains68000 registers, condition flags, memory-mapped STE hardware and dynamic resume dispatch. No interpreter is not equivalent to recovered high-level native game logic. Hold for architecture/scope audit.

title: Serial Experiments Lain — PSX C reconstruction and native client
reason: Matching game C and separate SDK-based host client. Inspected C defines recovered game/media structures; original PsyQ libraries are linked separately, not counted as newly decompiled game logic.

title: Rayman3 Readvanced — C# recreation
reason: MonoGame recreation of decompiled game behavior with typedactor/action code. README explicitly distinguishes recreation from matching decompilation. Under development with no official downloadable builds.

title: ADFS Tools — Filecore image manipulation
reason: E+ new-map/Filecore structures, fragment allocation, BigDir parsing and boot-loader preservation utilities. Current primary use is RISC OS Pi media, not every historical ADFS variant.

title: RISC OS ROM Tools — checksums and extension images
reason: RISC OS 3 ROM checksum/size repair, striping and 5th-column extraction/building. Inspected checksum code implements four interleaved CRC accumulators.

title: dcload-ip — Maple passthrough variant
reason: IP executable loader and PC-I/O bridge with added Maple passthrough. Inspected target command handlers implement network transfer and execution handoff.

title: Sensible World of Soccer — Amiga disassembly and analysis
reason: Amiga SWOS 96/97 analysis combines annotated assembly, generated C and IDA/Ghidra export and repair scripts. Generated decompiler C is not a finished native C port.

title: ZX Spectrum — browser tape and screen editor
reason: Single-file browser tool implements SCR conversion, BASIC tokenization, TAP/TZX generation, WAV synthesis/decoding and a limited Z80 assembler. Unsupported instruction forms explicitly fail; not a full assembler or hardware-fidelity claim.

title: djpoke/silverpong
reason: README explicitly calls it Amiga-like and programmed in AppGameKit Studio. No native Amiga implementation or specific reconstructed historical game established.

title: BitJag Atari Jaguar 240p Test Suite

title: EDAS 1.8 — recovered C128 editor/assembler

title: Gradle Retro Assembler Plugin — C64 build and asset pipeline

Selected KickAssembleAdapter constructs real compiler invocations; current source also contains CharPad, SpritePad, GoatTracker and image/flow modules. KickAssembler is the sole dialect claimed by README; presence of a flow module is not independent verification that every pipeline feature works. Native C64 output and host-side build orchestration are separate roles. AI-generated implementation and model-only/configuration evidence are distinguished.

title: LADS — reconstructed book-source assembler
reason: Reconstructs Richard Mansfield’s printed LADS assembler listings with OCR corrections, modern ca65 translation, machine/config overlays and object-code oracles. C64 generated source explicitly sets 6502 ISA and machine I/O equates; materialization scripts produce per-machine assembly/binary/disk artifacts. Root is substantive source reconstruction plus verification tooling; not simply a scanned-book archive. C64 VERIFY.txt reports 5,032 assembled bytes compared against a 4,986-byte oracle prefix, all matching. Do not call the entire binary byte-exact or independently verified. Disk images are documented as structurally validated but not emulator-boot-tested upstream. Apple from-source variant remains a study, with canonical decompiled variant retained. MIT applies only to original tools; reconstructed source/object code remains under original copyright. Raw book pages must be separately fetched.

title: Perihelion 2.0 — Amiga BBX game reconstruction
reason: Rebuilds Craig Dorrell’s Amiga BBX door game using surviving introduction, screenshots and original bitmap fonts; Python engine serves terminal and browser clients. Actual gameplay module implements movement, combat, economy, fleets and multiplayer state. Amiga-font parser recovers preserved glyphs into modern rendering assets. Historical README.TXT supports Amiga BBX origin; modern README.md carefully distinguishes surviving material from unavailable binary/full manual. No original game binary is available to this project: reconstruction includes inferred rules, naming choices, player recollections and modern additions, so it is not a binary-derived decompilation. No license found; original font/artwork is preserved rather than newly authored. Rights and full behavioral equivalence remain unverified. Repository description says 1988 while modern README specifically reconstructs the 1992 version 2.0; retain 1992 target and do not silently harmonize these dates.
